warnings: the canary is an over-privileged CALLER, not a deployed broken function: it proves the detector can see tenant data in a response, not that a subtle authorization bug would be caught. A deployed canary is gated on Andrew — ROADMAP 0.6.

public by design, measured rather than assumed: an ANONYMOUS caller holding a booking's UUID moved booking_services, bookings, business_invites, business_users, campaign_visits, customers, email_sends on the twin tenant. That is the UUID-bearer model cancel-booking and reschedule-booking are built on — the emailed link is the credential. It is not a tenant leak, and it is worth knowing that the UUID is the only thing protecting those rows.

platform-admin: owner A could not get a 2xx with its OWN tenant either (self(A) 404, anon 404, owner A 404, staff A 404, former A 404, service 404). NOT A TENANT GATE AT ALL, so making A's own call succeed would MANUFACTURE A WRONG ANSWER. It answers 404 to owner A because owner A is not a platform admin; the fix would be to make them one, and a platform admin legitimately sees every tenant, so the cross-tenant refusal this check is looking for could never appear. Its authorization needs a different instrument. Its 400 guards name nothing this harness is missing, so the refusal is elsewhere — a lookup, a permission, or a precondition on the row. Either way the cross-tenant refusal proves nothing and nothing is claimed.

send-email: owner A could not get a 2xx with its OWN tenant either (self(A) 401, anon 401, owner A 401, staff A 401, former A 401, service 401). INTERNAL RELAY, BY DESIGN. It compares the Authorization header against the service-role key and answers 401 to anything else, so no tenant actor can ever get a 2xx out of it. Its own comment says so: callable only with the service key, 'so this can never be abused as an open relay'. There is no tenant boundary inside it to test. Its 400 guards name nothing this harness is missing, so the refusal is elsewhere — a lookup, a permission, or a precondition on the row. Either way the cross-tenant refusal proves nothing and nothing is claimed.
